techStack: verbatimModuleSyntax: true — type-only imports must use `import type { ... }`
jsx: react-jsx (automatic transform) — no `import React` needed in component files
noUnusedLocals/noUnusedParameters: true — unused identifiers are compile errors
strict mode NOT explicitly enabled (but verbatimModuleSyntax + noUnused* are strict-adjacent)
Test runner: Vitest 3.2 + jsdom 26 + @testing-library/react 16; globals: true (no explicit imports of describe/it/expect)
Setup file stubs fetch globally before each test — API calls are always mocked
Build command: `tsc -b && vite build`; type-check is part of build
features: App.tsx: root orchestrator — wires useProductFilters hook into FilterPanel, SortSelect, Spinner, ProductList, pagination
FilterPanel.tsx: search input, category dropdown, in-stock checkbox, clear-filters button — no errors
ProductCard.tsx: renders image, name, category, truncated description, formatted price, discount badge, rating, tags, stock status — has discountPercent bug
ProductList.tsx: maps products array to ProductCard; shows empty-state message — no errors
SortSelect.tsx: four-option sort dropdown — has type mismatch on onChange
Spinner.tsx: minimal loading indicator with aria-label — no errors
useProductFilters.ts: manages filter state, pagination, and async fetchProducts — no errors
productFilters.ts: pure filterProducts function + FilterState type — no errors
formatters.ts: formatPrice (accepts discountPct?:number), formatRating, truncate — no errors
productsApi.ts: fetchProducts(page) calling localhost:3001/products — no errors (hardcoded token is a pre-existing issue, not in scope)
types/product.ts: Product (with discountPct?: number), PaginatedResponse<T>, Category — no errors
data/products.ts: 15 static mock products correctly using discountPct field — no errors

Must not regress: search, category filter, in-stock filter, sort (4 options), clear filters, pagination (prev/next), loading spinner, error alert, results count, empty state, discount badge + price formatting
architecture: Layers (bottom to top): types/ → data/ → api/ → utils/ → hooks/ → components/ → App.tsx
FilterState type lives in utils/productFilters.ts and is consumed by hooks/ and components/
Components use named exports for types (`import type { FilterState }`); default exports for component functions
All fixes are in the component/orchestrator layer — no changes needed in types/, utils/, hooks/, api/, or data/
Import pattern to follow: `import type { X }` for type-only imports; relative paths (no aliases)
edgeCases: App.tsx: The broken <ProductList> tag is never closed, making <div className='pagination'> appear to be inside its props — a JSX parse error that prevents the entire app from mounting, blocking all tests
App.tsx fix: adding `/>` makes <div className='pagination'> a sibling inside the enclosing fragment — correct intended structure, no further JSX restructuring needed
ProductCard.tsx: discountPct is optional (discountPct?: number) — the existing `!= null` guard on line 9 correctly handles both undefined and null, so the rename preserves optional semantics

ProductCard.tsx: formatPrice in formatters.ts uses `if (!discountPct)` (falsy check) — a value of 0 would be treated as no discount, but this is a pre-existing issue in formatters.ts not introduced by the rename
ProductCard.tsx: no test asserts discount badge text or discounted price values, so Fix 2 introduces no test regression
SortSelect.tsx: the `as FilterState['sortBy']` cast is TypeScript-only (no runtime change); option values in JSX are constrained to the four union members, making the cast safe
SortSelect.tsx: sorting.test.tsx uses userEvent.selectOptions with 'price-asc', 'price-desc', 'rating-desc' — all valid union members; fix unblocks compilation without changing assertion values
